title: Same Mac. New machinery.
caption: Contents replaced. Case: untouched.
footnote: The MacBook Air's fan has left the collection.

before.label: Intel chips
before.detail: Intel made the Mac's main processor from 2006.

change.label: Swap the chip
change.detail:
First M1 Macs: November 2020.
Last to switch: Mac Pro, June 2023.

after.label: Apple silicon
after.detail:
Apple designs the chip.
Processor, graphics and memory share one package.

before.label: Ran directly
before.detail: Apps were built for Intel and ran on Intel.

change.label: Translate with Rosetta 2
change.detail: Rosetta 2 converts Intel apps to run on the new chips.

after.label: Most still run
after.detail:
Most Intel apps work unchanged.
Kernel extensions and Intel virtual machines do not.

change.label: Ship universal apps
change.detail: One app file holds code for both chip families.

after.label: One download, both chips
after.detail: The Mac runs the half that fits. Nobody has to choose.

before.label: 12 hours of video
before.detail: Apple's rating for the early-2020 Intel MacBook Air.

change.label: Use less power
change.detail:
Four fast cores for heavy work.
Four frugal ones for everything else.

after.label: 18 hours of video
after.detail:
Apple's rating for the M1 MacBook Air.
No fan.

before.label: Boot Camp
before.detail: Intel Macs could restart into Windows.

change.label: Drop Boot Camp
change.detail: Boot Camp needs an Intel chip. It was not carried over.

after.label: Virtual machine only
after.detail: Windows 11 for Arm runs inside apps such as Parallels.
